messages.subject: CFA using COV
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying CFA with COV using test data(dichotomous) like this;

(1)
modelA<-mirt.model()
F1=1,2,3
F2=4,5,6
F3=7,8,9
COV=F1*F2*F3
resultA<-mirt(data,modelA,method="EM");resultA
summary(resultA)

Factor covariance: 
      F1    F2    F3
F1 1.000 0.947 1.000
F2 0.947 1.000 0.947
F3 1.000 0.947 1.000

(2)
modelB<-mirt.model()
F1=1,2,3
F2=4,5,6
F3=7,8,9
COV=F1*F2*F3
resultB<-mirt(data,modelB,method="MHRM");resultB
summary(resultB)

Factor covariance: 
      F1    F2    F3
F1 1.000 0.900 0.924
F2 0.900 1.000 0.916
F3 0.924 0.916 1.000

In (1), factor covariance F1*F3 is 1..so method"EM" can't calculate factor covariance three and over?
I think EM may use only 2 factors...

please give me your advice.

thank you.

It's only 1 because of rounding the summary function. To see a more exact value, use summary(mod, digits = 20), so something like that.

Either way, these correlations are extremely high, so it likely makes much more sense to treat the model as unidimensional rather than correlated multidimensional. Perhaps compare the fit of this model to a 1-factor model to see how much information is lost (though I doubt factors correlating this highly are adding much of anything to the model). Cheers.
